content:
- Overestimate prices after strong bullish sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.7 for 3+ consecutive days).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low or negative (sentiment < 0.3 or negative values).  
- Overshoot in early forecast periods (first 5–7 days) after recent price spikes — reduce initial forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- Lagged overreaction: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, forecast should drop 1–3% per day for 3–5 days, not just revert to mean.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate if sentiment is volatile or mixed — cap forecast at 10% above 30-day moving average.
